_meta.indication: RAPAFLO, an alpha-1 adrenergic receptor antagonist, is indicated for the treatment of the signs and symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). RAPAFLO is not indicated for the treatment of hypertension.

pivotal_trials.design: Multi-center, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, placebo-controlled, 12-week study with open-label extension, conducted at 42 sites in the US.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients aged ≥ 50 years with BPH (IPSS ≥ 13 and maximum urinary flow rate 4-14 mL/sec with minimum voided volume of 125 mL).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to week 12 in total IPSS score (primary); change in Qmax (secondary).
pivotal_trials.result: IPSS change: -6.7 Rapaflo vs -3.7 placebo (treatment difference -3.0; p<.0001). Qmax change: 2.2 Rapaflo vs 1.2 placebo (difference 1.0; p=.0060).

nct_ctgov.title: A New Drug for Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH) Compared With Placebo

pivotal_trials.design: Multi-center, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, placebo-controlled, 12-week study with open-label extension, conducted at 44 sites in the US; identical to SI04009 except no plasma concentration data collected.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients aged ≥ 50 years with BPH (IPSS ≥ 13 and maximum urinary flow rate 4-14 mL/sec with minimum voided volume of 125 mL).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to week 12 in total IPSS score (primary); change in Qmax (secondary).
pivotal_trials.result: IPSS change: -6.4 Rapaflo vs -3.4 placebo (treatment difference -3.0; p<.0001). Qmax change: 2.9 Rapaflo vs 1.9 placebo (difference 1.0; p=0.0431).

nct_ctgov.title: A New Drug for Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH) Compared With Placebo

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥ 2%): retrograde ejaculation (28.1% vs 0.9% placebo), dizziness (3.2% vs 1.1%), diarrhea (2.6% vs 1.3%), orthostatic hypotension (2.6% vs 1.5%), headache (2.4% vs 0.9%), nasopharyngitis (2.4% vs 2.2%), and nasal congestion (2.1% vs 0.2%).
target_moa: Silodosin is a selective antagonist of post-synaptic alpha-1 adrenoreceptors (binding with high affinity to the alpha-1A subtype) located in the prostate, bladder base, bladder neck, prostatic capsule, and prostatic urethra; blockade relaxes smooth muscle, improving urine flow and reducing BPH symptoms.

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the product is a member of the alpha-1-adrenergic receptor antagonist class and did not pose unique concerns beyond those applicable to other members of this class.

summary.text: Standard NDA under section 505(b) for silodosin (Rapaflo), a selective alpha-1 adrenergic receptor antagonist, approved for the signs and symptoms of BPH based on two identical 12-week placebo-controlled Phase 3 trials (SI04009 and SI04010); not referred to an advisory committee and pediatric study requirement waived.

citations.quote: Please refer to your new drug application (NDA) dated December 12, 2007, received December 13, 2008, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act for RAPAFLO® (silodosin) Capsules, 4mg and 8mg.

The applicant, Watson Laboratories, Inc. reports efficacy and safety data from two Phase 3 clinical studies (study SI04009 and study SI04010) to support Rapaflo 8 mg once a day for the treatment of signs and symptoms of BPH. Both studies were parallel-group, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, placebo-controlled studies, conducted under identical but separate protocol.
We are waiving the pediatric study requirement for this application.
